outgoingFlows.description: New human infections following bites from infectious mosquitoes; newly infected humans develop patent parasitaemia after a liver-stage delay, with a proportion developing symptoms.
Mass treatment of uninfected individuals moves them into temporary prophylactic protection.
Symptomatic infections progress to asymptomatic infection in the absence of treatment or after treatment failure.
Successful treatment of symptomatic infections moves individuals into the treated infectious state.
Asymptomatic patent infections progress to the subpatent state.
Mass treatment or screening-based treatment of asymptomatic infections moves individuals into the treated infectious state.

compartments.primaryName: Infectious and Undetectable by Standard Microscopy Humans

outgoingFlows.description: Screening-based treatment can target subpatent infections when PCR is used.
Treatment failures enter the asymptomatic infectious state.
After parasite clearance, treated individuals may enter a protected prophylactic state depending on drug half-life.

compartments.primaryName: Uninfected and Protected by Antimalarial Prophylaxis Humans

outgoingFlows.description: Loss of prophylactic protection returns individuals to the susceptible uninfected state.
Mosquitoes become infected after biting infectious humans.
Extrinsic incubation progression from exposed to infectious mosquitoes.
